issues.t: Front subframe rusts through
issues.sym: The car pulls to one side, the steering goes off-center, you hear grinding or clunking from the front, or a front wheel suddenly tilts inward.
issues.why: The front subframe (the cradle that holds the engine and lower control arms) rusts from road salt. Once it rots, the suspension mounting points can tear loose. Suzuki later sent dealers a reminder to inspect suspension parts for salt damage.
issues.next: If the car suddenly pulls hard, clunks or a wheel leans in, stop driving and have it towed. On any Esteem from a salt state, ask a shop to put it on a lift and check the subframe and control arm mounts for rust.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded securely (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The problem only shows up in a crash.
issues.why: On some 2002 cars the paint under the windshield did not stick well enough, so the glass might not stay in place in a crash. That fails the federal windshield mounting standard. Suzuki recall 03V223000.
issues.next: Check the VIN on the NHTSA recall site or with a Suzuki-trained shop. Inspection and any repair under the recall were free.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint can separate
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, loose or wandering steering, uneven front tire wear. In the worst case a front wheel collapses inward.
issues.why: The ball joints that connect the lower control arms to the steering knuckles wear out and, on rusty cars, can pull apart. Suzuki sent its US dealers a bulletin stressing regular inspection of the lower arm ball joints.
issues.next: Have the front ball joints checked at every tire rotation or inspection. If one is loose, replace it before driving further.

issues.t: Front strut or control arm comes loose
issues.sym: A loud pop from the front, sudden pulling to the right, shaking, a wheel that leans, or steering that stops responding.
issues.why: Owners report missing strut bolts, broken control arms and bent axles after potholes. Age and rust weaken these parts.
issues.next: Pull over safely and do not keep driving. Have it towed and get the front suspension inspected.

issues.t: Soft brake pedal or weak braking
issues.sym: The pedal feels soft or sinks, and the car takes longer to stop than it should.
issues.why: Owners report brakes that feel spongy or don't stop the car well. Air in the lines, a leak, a worn master cylinder or worn pads are common causes. Suzuki also issued a service manual correction for brake torque specs.
issues.next: Don't drive with a soft pedal. Have the brake fluid level, lines, calipers and master cylinder checked right away.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley or timing belt failure
issues.sym: A ticking or rattling noise at the front of the engine, then sudden loss of power or the engine stopping. Power steering can go heavy if the belts stop turning.
issues.why: Owners report the crankshaft pulley breaking at speed and damaging the timing belt, and one report of timing slipping after a ticking noise started. The timing belt also wears out with age.
issues.next: If a new noise starts at the front of the engine, get it checked soon. Replace the timing belt on schedule, and check the pulley and its bolt at the same time.

issues.t: Automatic transmission stuck in a low gear
issues.sym: The car won't shift up and stays in a lower gear, with a loud whine or roar at highway speed.
issues.why: Owners report the automatic getting stuck in a lower gear, in one case after three transmission replacements. Electrical faults can force a fail-safe mode, and internal wear can do the same.
issues.next: Avoid highway driving. Have a shop read transmission codes and check the fluid before replacing anything.

issues.t: Engine stalls or loses power while driving
issues.sym: The engine hesitates when you accelerate, or it dies in traffic and has to be restarted or towed.
issues.why: Owners report stalling and loss of power. Reported fixes included a fuel gauge sending unit, and dealers checked fuel tank sensors and the gas cap. Fuel delivery, sensor or ignition faults can all cause it.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer and brake firmly (power assist drops), get off the road and have it diagnosed. Note when it happens (hot, cold, low fuel) to help the shop.

issues.t: Sudden loss of all electrical power
issues.sym: Everything goes dead while driving: lights, dash and engine.
issues.why: One owner traced repeated total power loss to a loose 80-amp main fuse under the hood. A loose main fuse or battery connection cuts power to the whole car.
issues.next: Get safely off the road. Have the main fuse, fuse box terminals and battery cables checked and tightened.

issues.t: Oil leak from front crankshaft seal
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the engine, oil on the belts or lower engine, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The rubber seal around the crankshaft hardens with age and starts to leak, usually at high mileage. On the 1.6L the seal sits behind the timing belt, so the repair costs much more.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up. On the 1.6L, have the seal done at the same time as the timing belt to save labor.

issues.t: Steering wanders from worn inner tie rod
issues.sym: The car wanders on the highway, pulls one way and then the other, or the steering feels loose.
issues.why: A torn tie rod boot lets water and dirt into the inner tie rod joint, which then wears out. Owners also report wandering and pulling from other front-end wear.
issues.next: Have the tie rods and boots checked. Replace a worn tie rod and get an alignment.

issues.t: Key sticks in the ignition
issues.sym: The key won't turn or won't come out, and on automatics the shifter may not come out of Park.
issues.why: Owners report keys sticking in the ignition and shifters stuck in Park, often needing more than one repair. A worn lock cylinder or shift interlock is the usual cause.
issues.next: Don't force the key. Have the ignition lock cylinder and the brake-shift interlock checked.

issues.t: Check engine light comes and goes
issues.sym: The check engine light turns on and off, sometimes with no stored code.
issues.why: Owners report the light coming and going, and some code readers have trouble talking to these older cars. A loose gas cap, failing sensors or small vacuum leaks are common causes.
issues.next: Tighten the gas cap and have the codes read by a shop with a scan tool that supports the Esteem.

issues.t: Damaged vapor control valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on.
issues.why: Suzuki issued a bulletin saying some 2002 Esteems may have a damaged vapor control valve in the fuel vapor system. One owner had the light return after a first repair and needed another valve.
issues.next: Ask a Suzuki-trained shop about bulletin SC18 and have the fuel vapor system tested.

issues.t: Runs rough once warmed up
issues.sym: After the engine warms up it shakes and runs as if some cylinders are not firing.
issues.why: An owner reported this at about 43,000 miles. A misfire from ignition parts, injectors or contaminated fuel is the usual cause.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked soon, because a misfire can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Rotten egg smell from the exhaust
issues.sym: A sulfur or rotten egg smell from the tailpipe.
issues.why: An owner of a 1999 Esteem with the 1.8L reported this at about 80,000 miles and suspected the catalytic converter. A converter that is failing, or an engine running rich, gives off this smell.
issues.next: Have the engine checked for a rich-running condition first, then the converter.

issues.t: Hard to start, then dies when warm
issues.sym: The engine only starts with help and then stalls once it warms up.
issues.why: One owner reported this at about 89,000 miles. Fuel delivery, an idle air control fault or a failing temperature sensor can cause it.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure and engine sensors tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Transmission noise on the wagon
issues.sym: A whining or grinding noise from the transmission that gets worse with time.
issues.why: An owner of a 1999 Esteem wagon had the transmission replaced at about 33,000 miles, and the same noise came back at about 48,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level first. If the noise keeps getting louder, have the bearings and gears inspected before it fails completely.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsates when stopping
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses or the steering wheel shakes when you brake.
issues.why: The front rotors run out of true after heavy braking or uneven wheel nut tightening.
issues.next: Have the rotors checked. Resurfacing or replacing them, and tightening wheel nuts with a torque wrench, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Clutch wears out early
issues.sym: The engine revs but the car doesn't speed up, or the clutch engages very high.
issues.why: An owner of a 1998 Esteem reported early clutch failure.
issues.next: Have the clutch and its cable or adjustment checked. A slipping clutch only gets worse.

issues.t: Horn stops working
issues.sym: The horn doesn't sound, which can fail a state inspection.
issues.why: An owner reported the horn quitting. A bad horn, relay, fuse or the contact in the steering wheel is the usual cause.
issues.next: Check the horn fuse and relay first, then the horn itself.
